body:
## What happened

A queue claim was accepted with a 45-minute lease, then silently disappeared ~15 minutes later, so every subsequent checkpoint/heartbeat/complete for that task returned `task 11049 is not claimed by repo-worker-code` and the worker had to finish through the GitHub fallback path.

Timeline (all 2026-11-08Z):

- `09:40:06` — `repo-queue claim --queue repo-health-code-pilot --worker repo-worker-code --lease-seconds 2700 --lane 9aca43b4-...` returned task **11049** with `"lease_until": "2026-11-08T10:25:06Z"` and `"lane_id": "code-z"` (the passed lane id was not stored).
- `09:40:20` — `repo-queue checkpoint 11049 --worker repo-worker-code --stage claimed` succeeded.
- `09:57` — `repo-queue checkpoint ... --stage triaged` failed: `not claimed by repo-worker-code`; `heartbeat 11049` failed the same way; `repo-queue list --status claimed --limit 500` no longer lists it.
- The task was still not claimable afterwards: a new `claim` returned a different, older-by-priority task (11972) instead of 11049.

## Why this matters

The lease the caller asked for and the lease the row reported (`10:25:06`) does not match when the claim actually died (~`09:55`, i.e. ~900 s = the helper's default `--extend-seconds`/heartbeat window). A worker that trusts the reported `lease_until` will lose its claim mid-task and, as here, be forced onto the GitHub fallback for its closing verbs — the exact "claimed-then-abandoned" shape the anti-evaporation discipline exists to prevent.

## Hypothesis

Either (a) `claim` stores `lease_until` from `--lease-seconds` but the reaper / claim validity check uses `claimed_at + 900 s`, or (b) the `leases` table row is written with the default 900 s while `tasks.lease_until` keeps 2700 s, so the two disagree.

## To check

- `agent.tasks` vs `leases` rows for task 11049 (worker `repo-worker-code`) on 2026-11-08.
- The claim RPC's `lease_seconds` handling vs `expire_leases` / `heartbeat_task` lease checks.

Note: `"lane_id": "code-z"` on the claim, despite `--lane 9aca43b4-5439-4939-9f71-323f5d32521b`, may be the same class of "requested value not honoured" defect.

## Acceptance criteria
- A claim taken with --lease-seconds 2700 remains claimed for the full lease: checkpoint, heartbeat, and complete by the claiming worker succeed at any point before lease_until.
- The lane_id passed at claim is the lane_id stored on the task row (the 2026-11-08 claim stored a different lane than the one passed).
- A regression test or broker-level check pins lease duration + lane storage, so a silent ~900s claim death recurs detectably, not silently.
